+ Follow this systematic approach:

+ - Scan the conversation for primary topic indicators and domain signals
+ - Identify the temporal context and any explicit time references
+ - Determine the general conversation style and participant dynamics
+ 
+ ### 2. Domain Classification
+ - Identify the primary domain from the approved taxonomy
+ - Determine if a subdomain specification is warranted and available
+ - Consider secondary domains if the conversation spans multiple areas
+ - Assess the technical depth and specialization level
+ 
+ ### 3. Contextual Analysis
+ - Evaluate the conversation type based on structure and purpose
+ - Identify the life area context if clearly applicable
+ - Determine appropriate contextual tags from the approved list
+ - Consider suggesting a new contextual tag only if none fit and it's clearly needed
+ 
+ ### 4. Confidence Assessment
+ - Assign confidence scores based on clarity of evidence
+ - Use lower confidence (< 0.7) when indicators are ambiguous
+ - Remember that tags with confidence below 0.65 will be rejected
+ 
+ ## Classification Rules
+ 
+ **Strict Taxonomy Compliance**:
+ - Use ONLY approved tags from the taxonomies below
+ - Domain/subdomain pairs must exist exactly as specified
+ - For contextual tags, prefer approved options over new suggestions
+ 
+ **Confidence Scoring Guidelines**:
+ - **0.9-1.0**: Clear, unambiguous evidence with strong domain indicators
+ - **0.7-0.89**: Good evidence with minor ambiguity or some interpretation required
+ - **0.65-0.69**: Moderate evidence but reasonable confidence in classification
+ - **Below 0.65**: Insufficient evidence (tag will be rejected)
+ 
+ **Quality Standards**:
+ - Prioritize accuracy over completeness
+ - When uncertain between options, choose the more general classification
+ - Provide explanations for contextual tag suggestions or low confidence scores
